title: Quest: Query-Aware Sparsity for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
one_line_claim: Dynamic query-aware KV cache page selection achieves 7.03x self-attention speedup while maintaining lossless accuracy on long-context tasks.
method_summary: Quest maintains min/max key statistics per KV cache page and estimates page criticality using element-wise products with query vectors, loading only Top-K critical pages for attention computation. Unlike static eviction, retains all cached data and selects dynamically per query, preventing loss of tokens crucial for future queries.

key_findings.finding: Quest applies query-aware page selection to load only the top-K critical KV pages, accelerating self-attention while preserving accuracy on long-context tasks.
key_findings.quote: We propose Quest, a query-aware KV cache selection algorithm... Quest can achieve significant speedup with negligible accuracy loss.

key_findings.finding: Maintains lossless quality on passkey retrieval and LongBench while operating with a small fraction of the cache.
key_findings.quote: lossless on passkey retrieval and LongBench

relation_to_herald.shared: Both address KV cache compression in long-context LLM inference and operate at token/page granularity.
differs_on: Quest optimizes speedup via selective loading of critical pages; HERALD predicts catastrophic failure onset from per-token logit distributions.
Quest treats compression as a selection mechanism; HERALD operates downstream of any compressor and detects failure onset.
Quest uses min/max key statistics and query-product scoring; HERALD uses XGBoost on zero-cost logit features.
